name: Big Daddy Dave

tenures.source: Debuted by disqualification for throwing salt in Chris Williams's eyes on opening night; lasted well into the Second-Chance Royal Rumble seven weeks later.

caption: A brawler who opened the promotion's history by getting himself disqualified rather than losing cleanly, then chokeslammed his own opponent for good measure.

name: "Irish Heartbreak" Danny Flannagan

tenures.source: Lost the promotion's first main event to King Agony, then fell to "The Genius" Alfred Scarsone in the tournament's second round after a chair shot from a rival turned the match.

caption: A self-proclaimed superstar who walked to the ring with four valets called the Heartbreakers and twice fell just short of the promotion's own Unified World Championship picture.

name: "Sensational" Steven Green

tenures.source: Fought "The Genius" Alfred Scarsone to the promotion's own first-ever time-limit draw on opening night, then attacked him after the bell in frustration.

caption: An excitable newcomer whose opening-night draw against Alfred Scarsone left him so furious he kept fighting after the final bell.

name: "Boardwalk" Timothy Jensen

tenures.source: Beat "The Rebel" Tony Price on opening night, outlasted the Second-Chance Royal Rumble field to a still-unresolved double elimination with King Agony, then escaped a three-way steel cage over both Agony and Ian Walsh to reach the tournament's final four.

caption: A Monopoly-themed grinder who wrestled his way from an opening-night undercard win to the last cage standing, still unbeaten when the promotion's own record ends.

name: King Agony

tenures.source: Won the promotion's first main event with a Crucifix Powerbomb, later disguised himself as a rival gang's own masked enforcer to sneak into the Second-Chance Royal Rumble undetected until the very end.

caption: A half-masked monster billed from parts unknown who won the promotion's first main event, then spent forty minutes of its biggest battle royal wrestling in a rival's stolen mask before anyone realized who was under it.

name: Chris Williams

tenures.source: Had salt thrown in his eyes and was chokeslammed into the timekeeper's table on opening night; eliminated from the Second-Chance Royal Rumble weeks later.

caption: A face on the losing end of the promotion's first disqualification finish, thrown into the timekeeper's table for his trouble.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (chris-williams-gwf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: "The Rebel" Tony Price

tenures.source: Lost to "Boardwalk" Timothy Jensen on opening night and was the first man eliminated from the Second-Chance Royal Rumble weeks later.

caption: A self-styled non-conformist who never found his footing, opening and closing his run on the losing end of two of the promotion's biggest cards.

name: "The Genius" Alfred Scarsone

tenures.source: Fought to a time-limit draw on opening night, then defeated "Irish Heartbreak" Danny Flannagan in the tournament's second round with his Braincell Killer figure-four after a rival's chair shot turned the tide, becoming the promotion's own top-ranked wrestler.

caption: A cocky technician managed by "The Professor" Theodore Simmons who climbed to the promotion's own number-one ranking on the strength of a draw and a controversial second-round win.

name: David St. Clair

tenures.source: Lost his debut to "Human Torture Rack" Ian Walsh in a match a distracted referee nearly cost him, then lost to "Superstar" Ken Warren by countout after a self-inflicted fall onto the ringside steps.

caption: One of the promotion's first signees, undone twice by matches that got away from him rather than by his opponents' own finishers.

name: "The Greatest Ever" Shawn Walsh

tenures.source: Lost a tournament first-round match to "Boardwalk" Timothy Jensen, then was attacked in his own hotel room and unable to compete in his scheduled main event three weeks later.

caption: A tournament entrant whose own hotel-room assault, never solved in this record, cost him a shot at the promotion's own vacant Unified World Championship.

identity.note: Shares a bare name with three already-held wrestlers of the same name in other wings; nothing in this promotion's own record states an operator, hometown or history connecting any of them.

name: "Lightning Feet" Deon Langston

tenures.source: Wrestled Chris Williams to a disrupted finish when a rival tag team interfered, saved by a newcomer partner who became half of the tag team Ghetto Thunderstorm.

caption: A tournament also-ran whose interrupted match with Chris Williams led directly to the formation of the tag team Ghetto Thunderstorm.

name: "The Highland Wolf" Tim MacGregor

tenures.source: Advanced through the tournament's first round, then suffered a serious neck injury losing the second round to "The Enigma" Joe Hutchings's Michinoku Driver and dragon sleeper combination.

caption: A Scottish-born wrestler whose tournament run ended in a neck injury serious enough that the promotion's own broadcast called for medics on live television.

name: "Adamius Prime" Adam Mowery

tenures.source: Debuted with a Transformers-themed gimmick and a squirt-gun weapon, reached the Second-Chance Royal Rumble's final three, and defeated Anthony Mazzotta by submission in his final appearance in this record.

caption: A super-fan whose homemade Transformers gimmick and squirt-gun "blaster" carried him deeper into the promotion's own biggest battle royal than anyone expected.

name: "The Enigma" Joe Hutchings

tenures.source: Advanced through the tournament's first two rounds, injuring "The Highland Wolf" Tim MacGregor with a Michinoku Driver and dragon sleeper combination to reach the semifinal round.

caption: A question-mark-branded competitor who advanced two full tournament rounds without dropping a fall, injuring an opponent badly enough to end the man's own night.

name: "Ice Man" Craig Hudak

tenures.source: Won a dark match before the tournament proper began, then was written off the promotion's own record after a drunk-driving collision left him on life support, his tournament spot given away in the Second-Chance Royal Rumble.

caption: A tournament entrant whose own promotion held a televised moment of silence for him after a drunk-driving collision, before quietly clearing his spot for a Rumble to replace him.

name: "Crazy" Chris Hurt

tenures.source: Shared a three-way pinfall win over Trey Lawrenze with "Superstar" Ken Warren, then entered the Second-Chance Royal Rumble hiding a cattle prod inside a straitjacket before being tossed from the match.

caption: A straitjacketed brawler who smuggled a cattle prod into the promotion's own biggest battle royal before getting thrown out for his trouble.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (crazy-chris-hurt-rspwf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: "Superstar" Ken Warren

tenures.source: Shared a three-way pinfall win over Trey Lawrenze and "Crazy" Chris Hurt, then interfered in "The Genius" Alfred Scarsone's second-round tournament match by taking a chair from him and using it himself, setting up their own semifinal.

caption: A self-billed superstar managed by Keirn Von Holland who talked a feud with Alfred Scarsone into a semifinal booking by knocking him out with his own chair.

name: Trey Lawrenze

tenures.source: Lost a three-way match to a shared pinfall by "Crazy" Chris Hurt and "Superstar" Ken Warren after using a stun-gun on both opponents.

caption: A one-night entrant whose own stun-gun trick backfired when his two opponents pinned each other on top of him.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (trey-lawrenze-awmc); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.
Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (trey-lawrenze-iwe); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.
Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (trey-lawrenze-rspwf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: "Brutal" Brian Floyd

tenures.source: Debuted chasing Lance Younger with a steel chair, was eliminated from the Second-Chance Royal Rumble alongside a masked debuting rival, and got his revenge on that same rival five weeks later with a chair shot of his own.

caption: A hardcore-leaning newcomer whose feud with a mystery masked debutant ran from a shared Rumble elimination to a revenge chair shot weeks later.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (brian-floyd-ewc98); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.
Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (brian-floyd-gswp-1999); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: "Ladies Man" Vince Taylor

tenures.source: Entered the Second-Chance Royal Rumble swinging a chair, traded finishers with "The Lady Killer" Alex Thomas, and was eliminated by "Adamius Prime" Adam Mowery.

caption: A self-styled ladies' man whose Rumble entrance turned into a chair-swinging duel with a wrestler nicknamed for the opposite reputation.

name: "Mr. Everything" Tommy Hardbody

tenures.source: Debuted on the undercard, then lasted deep into the Second-Chance Royal Rumble before Big Daddy Dave eliminated him with a single clothesline.

caption: A confident debutant whose Royal Rumble run ended the moment Big Daddy Dave decided he'd had enough of him.

name: Ethan de Sade

tenures.source: Made a shocking Royal Rumble debut disguised as a second Ghost-Faced Killer, eliminating himself and "Brutal" Brian Floyd together with a clothesline over the top rope, then defeated "Contract Killer" Ker Avon by submission the following card.

caption: A hired hitman-styled debutant who announced himself by dressing as someone else entirely and taking a rival over the top rope with him.

identity.note: Shares a name with an already-held wrestler of the same name in another wing; nothing in this promotion's own record states an operator or history connecting the two.

name: "Contract Killer" Ker Avon

tenures.source: Debuted in the Second-Chance Royal Rumble and lost his singles debut to Ethan de Sade by submission after a distracted referee let the hold run long.

caption: A debuting hitman-gimmick wrestler whose whole record in the promotion is a single Rumble appearance and a lopsided singles loss.

name: Anthony Mazzotta

tenures.source: Debuted in the Second-Chance Royal Rumble, then lost by submission to "Adamius Prime" Adam Mowery in his only singles appearance in this record.

caption: A Canadian debutant who never got past his own return match against the promotion's own Transformers-gimmicked super-fan.

name: "Hot Ticket" Brant Johnson

tenures.source: Won his tag debut with partner Alex Thomas over the Teen Age Killers, later part of For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge's ongoing feud with two rival tag teams.

caption: One half of the tag team For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge, whose Extracurricular Activity powerbomb-neckbreaker combination won its debut against the Teen Age Killers.

name: "Lady Killer" Alex Thomas

tenures.source: Won his tag debut for For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge, entered the Second-Chance Royal Rumble, and lost the Ghetto Thunderstorm feud's rubber match by pinfall to Devon Henderson on the promotion's own last surviving card.

caption: One half of For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge, whose running feud with Ghetto Thunderstorm carried through the Royal Rumble to a final loss on the promotion's own last card.

name: Devon Henderson

tenures.source: Saved "Lightning Feet" Deon Langston from a tag-team ambush to help form Ghetto Thunderstorm, then won the team's feud with For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge by pinning "Lady Killer" Alex Thomas with his Thunderbolt nodowa bomb on the promotion's own last surviving card.

caption: A seven-foot powerhouse who formed Ghetto Thunderstorm on the spot to save a beaten wrestler, then closed out the feud he started.

name: Ghost-Faced Killer

tenures.source: A recurring masked member of the Teen Age Killers who ran through most of the Second-Chance Royal Rumble field before King Agony was revealed to have impersonated him from the opening bell; a Ghost-Faced Killer, presumed the genuine one, later ambushed both finalists of the promotion's own last surviving main event with a steel bar.

caption: A recurring masked enforcer whose own gimmick got borrowed for one memorable night by King Agony, who wrestled forty minutes of the promotion's biggest battle royal in the disguise before anyone noticed.

name: BMG

tenures.source: Debuted as a jobber on the undercard, then was eliminated from the Second-Chance Royal Rumble by Big Daddy Dave after a beer-fueled, foul-mouthed entrance.

caption: A profane, beer-drinking jobber billed as "Bald Mean Guy" whose Royal Rumble stay lasted about as long as his entrance music.

name: Themanwhoclaimshe'sbobdole

tenures.source: Lost his only match to "Human Torture Rack" Ian Walsh after a Bob Dole impersonation angle, including pinning Walsh to a two-count off a bridging German suplex before ultimately losing by pinfall.

caption: A one-off Bob Dole impersonator whose fan club of masked "Dole-ites" cheered him to a two-count before Ian Walsh finished him off.

name: Keirn Von Holland

tenures.source: Managed "Superstar" Ken Warren to the ring for his tournament second-round win over David St. Clair.

caption: A trenchcoated manager who accompanied "Superstar" Ken Warren through his tournament run.

name: "The Professor" Theodore Simmons

tenures.source: Managed "The Genius" Alfred Scarsone from the promotion's opening night through his tournament second-round win, repeatedly interfering at ringside on his charge's behalf.

caption: A toupeed manager whose ringside interference helped "The Genius" Alfred Scarsone through two rounds of the promotion's own title tournament.

name: Lance Younger

tenures.source: One of the promotion's two on-screen co-presidents, who booked the tournament, feuded openly with his own brother over the fed's direction, and was handcuffed to his own office wall by that brother on the promotion's own last surviving card.

caption: One half of a feuding pair of brother co-presidents, whose on-air power struggles over the tournament's own rules became as much a part of the show as the wrestling.

name: Dave Younger

tenures.source: The other of the promotion's two on-screen co-presidents, who overruled his brother's rulings repeatedly, allowed himself to be arrested on live television, and still made the deciding call on the promotion's own last surviving card.

caption: The more fan-favored of two feuding co-president brothers, who let himself be handcuffed and hauled off by police rather than back down from a ruling.

name: Chris Wilson

tenures.source: The promotion's lead play-by-play commentator across all five of its surviving broadcasts.

caption: The promotion's lead play-by-play announcer, seated between its two color commentators for the whole of its run.

name: Sam Braxton

tenures.source: A color commentator across all five of the promotion's surviving broadcasts, playing the traditionalist counterpart to "Merciless" Marc Mitchells.

caption: A self-described traditionalist commentator whose on-air disagreements with "Merciless" Marc Mitchells were a running bit of the broadcast.

name: "Merciless" Marc Mitchells

tenures.source: A color commentator and former wrestler across all five of the promotion's surviving broadcasts, playing the cynical counterpart to Sam Braxton.

caption: A former wrestler turned color commentator whose running jokes and one-liners carried much of the broadcast's own comic relief.

name: Kevin Del Corazon

tenures.source: The promotion's bilingual ring announcer across its surviving broadcasts.

caption: A bilingual ring announcer whose "mujeres y hombres" catchphrase greeted every broadcast of the promotion's own run.

name: Judy Dallas

tenures.source: The promotion's backstage interviewer on opening night, fending off unwanted advances from more than one wrestler.

caption: A backstage interviewer whose opening-night assignment mostly amounted to fending off the wrestlers she was sent to question.
